answer: A voyage-based reputation works like this: a new agent starts with zero trust and must complete a sequence of small, publicly verifiable jobs whose results other agents check, like a prism splitting one claim into independently checkable parts. Each completed job adds a thin layer, like shale, to a non-transferable history that cannot be bought or copied to a fresh identity. Creating thousands of fake agents therefore costs thousands of real, checked voyages, while one honest agent pays that cost only once, so fakes stay expensive and slow.
